rationale: Tier D is less about the kit being broken and more about opportunity cost: almost anything you invest into Orihime Inoue returns more on another character right now. As a Support, this build is judged by what it lets the rest of the team do — the picks below prioritize uptime, sustain, and buff coverage over personal damage. The Spirit damage type also matters here: content weak to it is where this build over-performs its tier, and content resistant to it is where you should bench accordingly.

The recommended set — Hidden Wisdom (3) — is chosen for how the set bonus lines up with the kit's actual damage profile, not because it's generically strong. Main stats go 1: HP%  •  2: HP%  •  3: HP% for the same reason: they feed what the kit multiplies. Survivability stats lead the priority: this kit needs to stay on the field to do its job, so HP/DEF return more than offensive lines would. Decent shield.

We call B0 the stopping point because that's where the boundary curve bends: the levels up to it unlock the pieces the kit is actually balanced around, while the levels past it mostly buy stat percentages at dupe prices. For free-to-play rosters that means settling at B0 and moving on; if dupes are no object, B1 is where the value per copy finally flattens out.
The featured rotation ("Shield Loop") is ordered the way it is to stack the kit's multipliers before the big hits land — the sequence matters more than the buttons.
Bond priority starts with Mayuri Bond because it feeds the stat the rest of this page is built around — later bonds are nice-to-haves, this one changes the math.

As with everything on this page, these calls come from community testing plus the wiki's numbers — when the data changes (balance patches, new stamps, better testing), the recommendations and this reasoning get updated together.
